# HLT-C12 extraction notes (A2)

## Rows proposed
- findings: 29 (N 17: F1-F16, F29; Q 12: F17-F28). transformations: 0. claims: 39. relations: 20 (backs 8, covers 12, clashes 0). decisions: header only.

## Scope choice
PLOS ONE has no "Conclusions" section. The final Discussion subsection "Implications" (p.11-12) is treated as the conclusions/recommendations section. The Discussion "Main findings" and "Methodological considerations" subsections are outside scope; they contain arguments relevant to claims, used below only where the Implications claim restates them.

## Look at first
1. Joint claims hinge on Rule 3 applied across sections. C18 (personal qualities are crucial determinants of alliance) and C35 (voluntary ward users had similar experiences to detained users) are stated in Implications without findings at that point; the findings are taken from the Discussion paragraphs that argue the same claim (p.10-11). C18 includes F8 (N: being ignored the most frequent staff-related negative event), used in the Discussion with "Similarly"; without F8, C18 is Q only. C35 includes F15 (N: detained users no less satisfied) and F24 (Q: voluntary users report similar restrictions), combined in one sentence on p.10-11. If A1 limits rests_on to the point where the claim is stated, both become empty-rests_on claims and the study has no joint claim.
2. C9 and C10 (abstract) are explicitly "Qualitative results suggest", so they are Q only even though the Discussion adds N corroboration (F8, F15).
3. Restatement claims (C11, C12, C16, C17, C37, C38) were treated under Rule 2: empty rests_on, linked by covers. Alternative: give them the findings of C1, C2, C6-C8. This choice does not change the joint count, since all are N only.
4. C13 (cannot exclude differences in service user characteristics) is a caveat; proposed as a claim resting on F16 and as covering C11 and C12 (Rule 4: narrows, both hold). A1 may judge it a limitation, not a headline claim.
5. C4 (self-rated recovery lower in crisis houses) is stated in the abstract without qualification, but the difference is not significant after adjustment (F4: 2.36, p = 0.51). Within-strand tension; no clash relation is possible since the adjusted result is not a headline claim.
6. C5 and F7: the text states that adverse events were more frequent on wards "for every negative event we asked about", but Table 4 shows "dismissed or ignored" by service users 23% vs 21% (p = 0.71) and staff "other" events 17% vs 4% higher in crisis houses. Reported inconsistency between text and table.
7. C19 (ward users experience a lack of compassion and humanity) cites only reference [35] at that point, but is introduced by "We further found"; rests_on proposed as Q findings F19-F22, whose wording matches ("a lack of care and compassion", p.7). Alternative: empty. The abstract recommendation C15 presupposes the same assertion; no relation C19-C15 proposed because the text does not link the two sections.
8. C29 (users can develop strong supportive peer relationships) rests on F3 (IPR) by measure match; the paper reports no qualitative peer findings.
9. C26 rests on F29 (staff backgrounds); strand N proposed because the reported form is counts (Table 6), though the Implications sentence reads as a setting description. A1 may judge F29 not a finding.
10. C6-C8 split by factor (Rule 1). The attenuation to non-significance (F14) is reached only with all three factors in the model; a single claim would rest on F9, F10, F12, F13, F14 (N only).

## Findings bearing on claims but not in rests_on (Rule 3)
- C33 (atmosphere): cites only [20]; F28 (p.10) reports the same contrast in the study's own data.
- C22/C23 (burnout): the Methodological considerations state "Qualitative interviews identified staff burnout as an important impediment" (p.11); F23 and F27 bear on this. Not linked at the Implications point.
- C21 (staff wrong for the job): F19, F20 bear on it; not linked.
- C34 (loss of liberty damaging): rests on F24, F26 by "our findings confirm"; it restates C10, no relation proposed.
- C39 and C14 (expansion of crisis houses) are close in content; the text does not link them.

## Relations
- No clashes proposed. C21 and C22 are presented as alternative explanations ("It is equally possible"); both can hold (Rule 4).
- R15 (C33 backs C32) rests on "For instance"; C33 illustrates rather than grounds C32. Borderline.
- R18-R20: "emerging explanation" read as covering the satisfaction model (C6-C8); it could also cover C9-C10.

## Transformations
None proposed. NES scores weighted by impact (weighting introduced at service users' suggestion, p.3) are a within-strand measure construction, not a transformation of registered findings. The qualitative component was designed to explain quantitative differences (p.6), but no conversion across strands is reported.
